findings.element: Reason line in How we get the data for non-clearing Stripe accounts (Stripe fees, Business Checking)
findings.finding: The line says there is a single Stripe clearing account, but the account list has two clearing accounts with automatic retrieval: "Stripe mzkt.by (required for Synder)" in USD and "Stripe mzkt.by · EUR". The line only points to the USD one.
findings.user_impact: A bookkeeper reconciling EUR activity follows the redirect to the USD clearing account. The run then covers the wrong currency's clearing account, and the EUR clearing account is never reconciled for the period.
findings.suggested_fix: Say the Stripe clearing accounts, plural, and name both, e.g. "…only available for Stripe clearing accounts. Upload the Stripe file for this account, or pick “Stripe mzkt.by (required for Synder)” or “Stripe mzkt.by · EUR” instead." Or point to the clearing account in the chosen account's currency.

evidence.quote: Automatic retrieval is only available for the Stripe clearing account. Upload the Stripe file for this account, or pick “Stripe mzkt.by (required for Synder)” instead.
evidence.source: Domain fact: one run = one clearing account, and the automated group is the integration's clearing account(s). The same screen's automated group lists both "Stripe mzkt.by (required for Synder)" and "Stripe mzkt.by · EUR", and both show "Automatic file retrieval Recommended".

findings.finding: The tooltip calls the data source "the platform", which vocabulary.md bans in favour of Integration. It also names the accounting company ("QuickBooks") where the ledger (Books) is meant.
findings.user_impact: "The platform" can be read as Synder itself, so it is unclear which two data sets the period filters. That matters for deciding whether boundary-date items are in scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as "Compares transactions dated in this range in your books and in the integration." or name the integration, e.g. "…in your books and in Stripe."

evidence.quote: Compares transactions dated in this range in QuickBooks and on the platform.
evidence.source: vocabulary.md, UI Words: "Integration | payment platform, sales platform, provider, system" and "Books | … the data/ledger inside the accounting company"

findings.finding: Both groups label the accounts "Synder accounts", but they are accounts in the QuickBooks chart of accounts. Examples are "Business Checking", "Business Checking · EUR", "Stripe fees" and "PayPal sales", and none of them are Synder-owned.
findings.user_impact: Calling them Synder accounts blurs the line between Synder and the books. A bookkeeper may think they are reconciling a Synder-side record rather than a general ledger (GL) account in the client's books, and a bank account like Business Checking looks as if Synder created it.
findings.suggested_fix: Label the groups by where the account lives and how its data arrives, e.g. "Clearing accounts (automatic retrieval)" / "Other accounts in your books (file upload required)". Keep the current wording only if production uses exactly this label.

evidence.source: vocabulary.md: "Books = the data/ledger ('synced to your books', 'transactions in your books')". Accounting rule: the account to reconcile is a chart-of-accounts account in the accounting company.

gaps: Results screen not exercised. With no matched/unmatched view, I can't check whether the period filter applies the integration timezone ("Timezone: Europe/Minsk") to QuickBooks transaction dates, which have no timezone. That could push items near month-end into false unmatched.

Retrieval failure and empty-result states are not implemented. The KF-9 preconditions (closed period, lost QBO auth, multi-currency off, missing mappings) are never shown, so I can't judge whether a run against a closed period is refused or explained.
No state with an overlapping period for the same clearing account, so the domain rule that periods can't overlap is not verified anywhere.
Stripe Assisted how-to path "In Stripe, open Balances → Balance change from activity." was not checked against a real Stripe Dashboard screen. Confidence is below the floor, so it is not raised.
